Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

overall adverb

taking everything together

also all in all, on the whole, in short, in all, basically, in a word, to cut a long story short, briefly, to put it briefly, make it brief!, to be brief, needless to say, what more can I say?, in one word

classical

Cic. Att. 14.1.1; Off. 1.149 (Lewis & Short, s.v. summa)
Hor. Ep. 1.1.106 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 107: in short, in summā, ad summam

ad summam

adverbial phrase

on the whole, in short

Sums up what has been said: “all in all, in a word”. Common in Cicero’s letters and in talk (Petronius’ freedmen).

Other words

  • in summā — in all, in total

    adverbial phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Q. Fr. 2.16.3: in summā quattuor sententiīs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 107: in short, in summā

    Of a count: “in all”. In post-Augustan prose also “at last”.

  • omnīnō — altogether, in all

    adverb · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. omnīnō; Traupman 270

    “Altogether, at all”; with numbers “in all, only”. For the adjective (“the overall picture”) use tōtus or ūniversus (see whole).

  • quid multa? — in short, basically (what more need I say?)

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Q. Fr. 2.7.3: quid multa? tenent omnia; Cic. Att. 7.4.3: quid multa? nihil mē aliud cōnsōlātur nisi quod …

    The speaker’s “basically”: it cuts a story short and goes to the point. So too quid plūra? and nē multa (Lewis & Short, s.v. multus).

  • ut in pauca cōnferam — to put it briefly

    also used · classical · Cic. Caecin. 17 (Lewis & Short s.v. ut); Traupman 94

    “To gather it into a few (words)”; to someone else, in pauca cōnfer!, make it brief! (Plaut. Poen. 5.4.54, Lewis & Short s.v. paucus).

  • ut breviter dīcam — to put it briefly

    also used · modern · Traupman 94

    Traupman’s phrase, of classical words; not found as a phrase in Lewis & Short or the loci.

  • quid quaeris? — in short, needless to say (what more do you want to know?)

    question standing apart from the sentence · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.1.2: quid quaeris? biduō factus est mihi familiāris (Lewis & Short s.v. quaerō); Traupman 104: needless to say, quid quaeris?

    A turn of Cicero’s letters, like quid multa?: it cuts the story short. Lewis & Short also gives nōlī quaerere (Cic. Fam. 4.4.3).

  • prōrsus — in a word, in short

    also used · classical · Sall. (Lewis & Short s.v. prōrsus); Traupman 270

Examples

  • ad summam, quotīdiē mē solēbam ad illum mētīrī

    in short, I used to measure myself against it every dayPetr. 75.2

  • quid multa? tenent omnia

    basically, they control everythingCic. Q. Fr. 2.7.3

  • Ad summam, bene nōbīs fuit.

    All in all, we had a good time.composed

  • ut in pauca cōnferam, testāmentō factō mulier moritur

    to put it briefly, the woman makes her will and diesCic. Caecin. 17 (Lewis & Short)

  • In pauca cōnfer!

    Make it brief!Plaut. Poen. 5.4.54 (Lewis & Short)

See also whole, total, in general.
